text:
tiny-voca

tiny-voca is a small English text-to-speech model. It has two voices, 4.5M
parameters, and runs on a CPU or in the browser.

Demo · Weights · Dataset

 Features

- Small : 4,537,291 parameters, 18 MB, waveform generator included.
- Fast : about 70x real time on four CPU threads.
- Two voices : F2 (female) and M2 (male), American English, 24 kHz.
- Runs anywhere : PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime Web.
- Open : code, weights, training recipe and dataset. Trained from scratch.

 Install

 

 Usage

 

 Option Default Meaning 
 --- --- --- 
 --text-file Read the text from a file instead of --text 
 --voice F2 F2 or M2 
 --speed 1.0 Speaking rate 
 --pitch-shift 0 Raise or lower the pitch 
 --pitch-range 1.0 More or less pitch movement 

Long text is fine. It is read one sentence at a time and the audio is joined.
A text that ends without a mark gets a full stop, so the last word does not
break off. A sentence with nothing to read, such as one in another script, is
skipped. The output never peaks above 0.99, so it does not clip as a 16-bit
WAV. In Python, tiny voca.infer.speak text does the same.

 ONNX

 

 --optimized writes a smaller graph with the same audio, up to float
rounding. In ONNX Runtime on a CPU it is about 10% faster on a 3-second
sentence and 25 to 40% faster on a 10-second one. It needs opset 16 or later.

A ready file is in the weights repository as onnx/model.onnx . The
model card shows how to call it.

 Web demo

The demo runs the model in the browser. It
plays each sentence as soon as it is made, and keeps the whole clip in the
player. Its source is in web/ .

 

 Plain JavaScript

An experiment in js/ : the model and the phonemizer in plain scripts, with no
libraries. It reads one 8 MB file and runs in the browser, in Node and in Bun.

 

See js/README.md.

 Training

 

The released weights took 7.7 hours on one RTX 4090. More about the model and
the data is in docs/model.md.

 Tests

 

 Limits

- English only. Two fixed voices. No voice cloning.
- The F2 voice sounds younger than intended. A more mature voice is planned.
- Foreign names and odd spellings are often read wrong.
- No streaming yet.

 Community

Built by other people on top of tiny-voca.

Languages and voices:

- apptor-tiny-tts: German.
- apptor-tiny-tts-at: Austrian German, with an accent you can turn up or down and a browser demo.
- tiny-voca-de-en: German and English, with up to 32 voices in each.
- tiny-voca-nl: Dutch, one voice, trained from scratch on an M4 Pro in about 5 hours, with a browser demo.
- tiny-voca-it: Italian.
- vocina: Italian, with a browser demo.
- zerre-tts: Turkish.
- clarvia-tts-tiny: Turkish, ten voices, with its own phonemizer for numbers, dates and money.
- tiny-voca-uzbek-navoiy: Uzbek, one male voice, trained from scratch on 7.7 hours of Navoiy-generated speech.
- korean-tts: Korean, and Korean mixed with English.
- tiny-voca-ja-tsukuyomi-chan: Japanese, in Tsukuyomi-chan's voice, under that voice's own terms.
- tiny-voca-ja: Japanese, two voices, trained on synthetic speech only.
- tiny-voca-zh: Mandarin Chinese, two voices, trained on synthetic speech only.
- tiny-voca-zh: Chinese, with male ( M ) and female ( F ) voices and a dedicated Chinese text front end.
- slyszeglosy: Polish.
- tiny-voca-ru: Russian, with a browser demo.
- tiny-voca-gr: Modern Greek, a male and a female voice.
- mini-voz: Spanish, with a Castilian accent.
- tiny-voca-es: Spanish from Spain, with a browser demo.
- alpa-es: Rioplatense Spanish.
- tiny-voca-fr: French, with a browser demo.
- tiny-voca-ptbr: Brazilian Portuguese, with its own phonemizer.
- tiny-voca-ptbr-kokoro: Brazilian Portuguese, with Kokoro's Brazilian voices as the teacher.
- tiny-broca: Brazilian Portuguese, two voices, reads letters with no dictionary, with a browser demo.
- tiny-voca PT-PT: European Portuguese, two voices, trained from scratch on 22.8 hours of synthetic speech, with a rule-based phonemizer and a browser demo.
- tiny-voca Arabic: Modern Standard Arabic, trained on a CPU from the Arabic Speech Corpus.
- tiny-voca-ar: Modern Standard Arabic, an early version with a browser demo.
- tiny-voca-arabic: Modern Standard Arabic, trained from scratch, with a browser demo.
- tiny-voca-he: Hebrew, one male voice, with a browser demo.
- pitput: Hebrew, eight delivery styles and expression tags like laughs and sighs, for research use only.
- Browser Voice: Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Malayalam and Telugu in native script or Roman letters, with a browser demo and its code.
- tiny-swara: Bengali, two voices, trained from scratch on free Kaggle GPUs.
- tiny-voca-hindi: Hindi, one voice with eight speaking styles, and a C++ engine.
- tui-voice-mini-ml: Malayalam, an early preview.
- tiny-voca-sinhala: Sinhala, a male and a female voice, trained from scratch on free Kaggle GPUs, with a browser demo.
- tiny-urdu: Roman Urdu, with a browser demo.
- Kurdish Behdînî Voice: Kurdish Behdînî, 21 voices, with a browser demo.
- tiny-ava: Persian (Farsi), one female voice, trained from scratch on about 20 hours of synthetic speech, with a browser demo.
- tiny-voca Kiswahili: Swahili, runs offline on a low-end Android phone.
- tiny-voca-lg: Luganda, two voices, with a rule-based front end and a browser demo.
- SobbieTTS: English, an expressive voice.
- alpa: Sanskrit, fine-tuned from tiny-voca on a CPU.
- fiato: English, with sighs, exhales and gasps.

Ports and apps:

- llama.cpp: runs tiny-voca with llama-tts , from GGUF files.
- voca: a rewrite in Rust.
- tiny-voca-rust: another Rust port.
- audio.cpp: runs tiny-voca in C++ with ggml.
- voca-server: a server with an OpenAI-compatible API.
- tiny-voca-esp32s3: runs on an ESP32-S3 microcontroller.
- tiny-voca-ane: runs on the Apple Neural Engine with Core ML, with a Swift package.
- tiny-voca-dashboard: a local dashboard.
- tinyvoca: a Mac app.
- CopySpeech: reads your clipboard aloud, with tiny-voca as the default voice.
- Tiny Reader: a Firefox add-on that reads web pages

install.title: Install
install.html:
git clone https://github.com/n4ze3m/tiny-voca.git
cd tiny-voca
pip install -e ".[own]"
hf download n4ze3m/tiny-voca --local-dir weights
export DIZIONE_DATA=weights/phonemizer

usage.title: Usage
usage.html:
python -m tiny_voca.infer \
  --checkpoint weights/tiny-voca.pt \
  --voice F2 \
  --text "Hello! This is tiny voca." \
  --output hello.wav
Option Default Meaning
--text-file Read the text from a file instead of --text
--voice F2 F2 or M2
--speed 1.0 Speaking rate
--pitch-shift 0 Raise or lower the pitch
--pitch-range 1.0 More or less pitch movement

Long text is fine. It is read one sentence at a time and the audio is joined. A text that ends without a mark gets a full stop, so the last word does not break off. A sentence with nothing to read, such as one in another script, is skipped. The output never peaks above 0.99, so it does not clip as a 16-bit WAV. In Python, tiny_voca.infer.speak_text does the same.
